# Critique — Pattern 3 (Musculoskeletal)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Joint Conditions (~7%), Spine (~5%), Bone (~3%), Muscle (~3%), Acute Injuries (~3%), Surgical History (~5%), Mobility & Functional Status (~5%), Connective Tissue (~2%), Foot Health (~3%), Self-Care (~4%), and the remainder consisting of specific orthopedic details and self-care fillers. A significant portion of the self-care and specific symptom questions (positions 99–255) felt forced to reach the exact 255-question limit; had the limit been smaller, we would have focused strictly on major diagnoses and functional mobility. Overlap occurs with Fitness History and Recent Medical Activity (e.g., strength routines, recent injury history, physical therapy) because joint integrity dictates safe physical activity boundaries and recovery progress. The V-flag was applied to questions where a "Yes" indicates protective self-care or active joint-preservation habits (e.g., core strengthening, ergonomics, using orthotics) to align with a convention where a stored bit `1` reflects risk, pain, or functional impairment. We paraphrased elements of the Oswestry Disability Index, the Beighton Score for hypermobility, and FRAX; clinicians should consult these official instruments for diagnostic scoring. The weakest question is position 255 ("Do you take a turmeric or curcumin supplement...") as supplement use is inconsistent and clinically secondary. No prior questions existed for Pattern 3 in `patterns.json`, enabling a clean, custom draft.
